# Stationary cap Hessians have no universal sign

This note concerns an ordinary convex body K in R^d, d>=2, with 0 in
its interior. It proves exact second-variation formulas and constructs
convex polytopes realizing every Hessian signature at any prescribed
stationary cap fraction. It does not construct a balanced circuit of
several such sections, and proves no mixed-integer depth bound.

Write coordinates as (z,t) in R^k x R, k=d-1, V=|K|, and

    Q_t={z:(z,t) in K},
    S(t)=|Q_t|,
    M_1(t)=integral_Qt z dz,
    M_2(t)=integral_Qt zz^T dz.

## 1. The regular second-variation formula

Put F(h,b)=V^(-1)|K intersect {t+h dot z>=b}|. If the section near
t=0 has C^2 boundary transverse to the t-coordinate, the usual graph
parameterization and differentiation under the integral give

    F_h(0,0)=M_1(0)/V,          F_b(0,0)=-S(0)/V,

and the full Hessian in (h,b) is

    (1/V) [ -M_2'(0)   M_1'(0) ]
          [  M_1'(0)^T -S'(0)   ].                         (1)

Here is a way to track every sign. In the distributional notation for
the one-variable Heaviside function, F is the integral of
1_{t+h dot z-b>=0}. Its first derivatives insert z delta(t) and
-delta(t); second derivatives insert zz^T delta'(t), -z delta'(t),
and delta'(t), respectively. Integration in t makes these
-M_2'(0), +M_1'(0), and -S'(0). Under the stated transverse C^2
assumption the same identities follow by ordinary differentiation in
boundary charts, so no distributional regularity assertion is needed.

In particular, for p(h)=F(h,0), the section Q_0 has centroid 0 if
and only if p is stationary at h=0. At such a section,

    Hess p(0)=-M_2'(0)/V.                                  (2)

The chart normal (h,1) is not a unit vector, but the represented
halfspace is unchanged by positive rescaling. At a critical direction
the chart Hessian agrees with the spherical Hessian in its orthonormal
tangent coordinates.

If N=(N_z,N_t) is the outer unit normal on the boundary of K along
the section, transversality gives |N_z|>0. The outward normal speed
of the boundary of Q_t is -N_t/|N_z|. The transport formula therefore
rewrites (2) as

    Hess p(0)=(1/V) integral_boundary Q0
                         zz^T N_t/|N_z| dH_(k-1).          (3)

None of (1)--(3) is asserted at arbitrary nonsmooth degeneracies.
The next construction gives a direct analytic proof for the specific
nonsmooth polytopes used below, without invoking that regularity.

## 2. An exact convex box-frustum construction

Let c_1,...,c_k be arbitrary real numbers. Choose positive heights
ell_minus,ell_plus such that 1+c_i t>0 throughout
[-ell_minus,ell_plus], for every i. Define

    K={ (z,t): -ell_minus<=t<=ell_plus,
                   |z_i|<=1+c_i t for all i }.

All defining inequalities are linear. Thus K is a compact convex
polytope with 0 in its interior. Set Q=[-1,1]^k,

    J(t)=product_i(1+c_i t),       C=sum_i c_i.

Its horizontal sections are diagonal images of Q, all with centroid
0. Consequently

    V=2^k integral_(-ell_minus)^ell_plus J(t)dt,
    p(0)= integral_0^ell_plus J(t)dt /
                         integral_(-ell_minus)^ell_plus J(t)dt. (4)

For the tilted cap make the change of variables
z_i=(1+c_i t)v_i, v in Q. Define

    A=sum_i h_i v_i,             B=sum_i h_i c_i v_i.

The cut inequality becomes t(1+B)+A>=0. Uniformly for v in Q and
all sufficiently small h, its lower threshold is inside the height
interval and equals

    tau=-A/(1+B)=-A+AB+O(|h|^3).

The tilted cap volume is exactly

    integral_Q integral_tau^ell_plus J(t)dt dv.

Using J(0)=1 and J'(0)=C, its difference from the untilted volume is

    integral_Q [A-AB-(C/2)A^2]dv+O(|h|^3).

The linear term vanishes. Symmetry gives zero mixed second moments
and integral_Q v_i^2=2^k/3. Hence p is analytic near 0 and

    Hess p(0)=-(2^k/(3V)) diag(C+2c_1,...,C+2c_k).           (5)

This also verifies (2) directly: M_2(t) has diagonal entries
(2^k/3)J(t)(1+c_i t)^2.

## 3. Any Hessian signature at any cap fraction

Let A be any symmetric k by k matrix, with eigenvalues a_i. Set

    c_i=-a_i/2+tr(A)/(2(k+2)).

Then C=-tr(A)/(k+2), so C+2c_i=-a_i. Rotate the z coordinates
by an orthogonal eigenbasis of A. Formula (5) now gives

    Hess p(0)=(2^k/(3V)) A.                                (6)

The scalar factor is strictly positive.

For any prescribed alpha in (0,1), choose L>0 sufficiently small
that all widths remain positive on [-L,L]. Choose
ell_minus=epsilon>0 so small that

    alpha/(1-alpha) integral_(-epsilon)^0 J(t)dt
                                      < integral_0^L J(t)dt.

The upper integral is a continuous strictly increasing function of
its upper endpoint. There is therefore a unique ell_plus in (0,L)
for which the upper integral equals alpha/(1-alpha) times the lower
integral. Equation (4) gives p(0)=alpha exactly.

As epsilon tends to zero, ell_plus and V tend to zero. Thus, at the
same fixed fraction alpha and with the same matrix A, the positive
factor in (6) can tend to infinity. In particular every prescribed
stationary cap fraction admits strict angular minima, strict angular
maxima, or any indefinite nondegenerate Hessian signature allowed
by k. This is an individual-section statement.

## 4. Three rational three-dimensional examples

Take d=3, ell_minus=1/4 and ell_plus=1/100. In all three examples,
Q_0=[-1,1]^2, so the cut t=0 is proper and has section centroid 0.
Its closed positive cap is {t>=0}; the plane has zero 3-volume.

* c=(1,1): V=304213/375000,
  p=30301/608426, Hess p=-(16/(3V)) I_2.
* c=(-1,-1): V=491413/375000,
  p=29701/982826, Hess p=+(16/(3V)) I_2.
* c=(1,-1): V=382187/375000,
  p=29999/764374, Hess p=diag(-8/(3V),8/(3V)).

All widths are positive and all cap fractions are less than 1/10,
hence less than gamma_3=27/64. The first cap is a strict angular
maximum, the second a strict angular minimum, and the third a saddle.
The companion Fraction verifier checks the volumes and fractions.

## 5. No scalar transform of cap fraction is a universal support function

Let phi be a nonconstant C^2 function on (0,1). There cannot be a
universal assertion that h_K(u)=phi(p_K(u)) is the support function
of a convex body for every K containing 0 in its interior, where
p_K(u)=|K intersect {u dot x>=0}|/|K| for unit u.

Indeed choose alpha with phi'(alpha) nonzero. At a stationary
direction with p_K=alpha, the support-function curvature condition
would require

    phi'(alpha) Hess_S p_K + phi(alpha) I >=0.              (7)

This condition follows by restricting the positively homogeneous
extension of a C^2 support function to any line tangent to the sphere;
its second derivative is Hess_S h+h I and must be nonnegative.
Construction (6) permits a Hessian with an eigenvalue of sign
opposite to phi'(alpha), whose magnitude tends to infinity while
alpha remains fixed. It violates (7). This excludes only potentials
depending on the direction through that single scalar p_K(u).
It does not exclude potentials involving full section moments.

## 6. Limits of a rank-reduction strategy

A nondegenerate stationary cap is an isolated angular critical point
of the fixed body, by the inverse function theorem applied to its
gradient. Thus a continuous local rotation preserving stationarity
need not be available. Body variation could still supply such a
deformation; (5) does not settle that question.

There is also no unconditional operation that reduces every balanced
stationary circuit to rank at most two without increasing its weighted
cap mean. For a tetrahedron and its centroid, the four vertex-side
planes parallel to the opposite facets have section centroid equal
to the body centroid. Symmetry in barycentric coordinates gives a
positive balanced circuit of rank three and cap mean 27/64.
The independently proved rank-two theorem in
`candidate 3ed6256a0896f434` gives mean
at least 3/7 for every rank-at-most-two stationary circuit in a
three-dimensional convex body. Since 3/7>27/64, a universal operation
with the claimed monotonicity would contradict that example.

A reduction conditioned on a strict violation of 27/64 is not
refuted by this equality example. Neither the Hessian construction
nor this observation supplies a low-mean balanced higher-rank
circuit; the joint problem remains separate.
